title: get_user() breaks for any non-numeric user_id
body: user_id: str is interpolated unquoted into the SQL string via f-string. sqlite3.Connection.execute() supports parameter binding (execute(sql, params)) but this bypasses it entirely. Any string id that is not a bare integer literal (e.g. a UUID, or an id containing a hyphen or letter like 'user-42') produces malformed SQL and raises sqlite3.OperationalError — the function is broken for the exact input type its own signature declares. Fix: cur.execute("SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ?", (user_id,)).

title: New query functions have no tests
body: get_user() and list_active() are new, non-trivial database-access behavior (including a query-construction path that is easy to get wrong, as the f-string bug on line 7 shows) and ship with no accompanying test exercising them against a real or in-memory sqlite3.Connection. Add at least a happy-path test per function and one covering a non-numeric id for get_user().
